rejected.title: Speciation
card: Speciation is the formation of new species. It happens when populations of one species are isolated, so they stop interbreeding and their gene pools diverge.
Each population faces different selection pressures and different chance changes in alleles. Over time they become so different that they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring.
Allopatric
populations are separated by a physical barrier or distance. Finches on different Galapagos islands diverged this way.
Sympatric
a new species forms in the same place, with no physical barrier. Two palm species on Lord Howe Island formed this way, in part by growing in different soils.
rejected.remember: Isolation stops gene flow, so populations diverge. Allopatric has a physical barrier, sympatric does not.

a.q: What must happen between two populations for them to become separate species?
opts: They stop interbreeding and diverge genetically
They move to separate islands and stay there
They grow larger than the original species
They gain new alleles from each other
a.why: Speciation needs gene flow to stop so the gene pools diverge. Separate islands are tempting, but that is only one way of isolating populations, as sympatric speciation occurs in one place.
a.clue: Think about what happens to the gene pools.

b.q: A drought dries the river joining two parts of a lake in Tasmania, leaving its fish in two separate ponds. Over time, the two groups can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring. What type of speciation is this?
opts: Allopatric, as dry land became a barrier between them
Sympatric, as the fish all began in the same lake
Sympatric, as no fish swam away to a new area
Not speciation, as the fish were never moved apart
b.why: The dry land between the ponds is a physical barrier that stopped gene flow, which is allopatric speciation. Starting in one lake does not make it sympatric, because sympatric speciation happens with no physical barrier at all.
b.clue: Could fish cross from one pond to the other?

problems.detail: The scenario is confusing: it says a lake 'has a river dry up and split a fish population into two ponds', which does not clearly explain how a lake becomes two separated ponds. It could read as 'A drought dries the river joining two parts of a lake, leaving the fish in two separate ponds.' The option 'Allopatric, as the fish moved to a new place' also names the right type with a wrong reason, which may catch students who stop at the first word.
